To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the band gap of CdS in layered hybrid CdS/surfactant composites is dependent of the length of the alkyl chain of the surf actant and the concentration in the inorganic layer of the sulphide.

a) the electronic structure of CdCl2/Cds nanocomposites is similar to that expected for a semiconductor confined between two surfactant layers; b) the band gap of the nanocomposite depends on both the concentration of sulphide ions and the length of the surfactan hydrocarbon tail and c) the nanocomposite shows a higher photocatalytic activity than "bulk" CdXx(OHS)y(CnTA).z.

the semiconducting properties (band gap, photocatalytic activity) of the CdS in the hybrid nanocomposites depend on both the length and the concentration of CdS in CdS/CdCl2 ultra-thin sheets, and that CdS/CdS/CdCl3/CnTA nanocomposites show better photocatalytic activity than "bulk" CdCl2/CnTA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterisation of hybrid inorganic-organic materials based on layered compounds.
the preparation of hybrid nanocomposites based on layered CdXx(Oh)y(CnTA)x and the study of their semiconducting properties.

the synthesis and characterization of a series of hybrid CdS/CdCl2/CnTA layered nanocomposites, where the CdCl2/CnTAB layers can be exchanged by CdS, and the effect on their semiconducting properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CdXx(OxH)y(CnTAC)z nanocomposite materials are a new class of semiconductor nanomaterials, which can be prepared by a solid phase/gaseous reaction, and are constituted by a CdXx(O)H)y layer sandwiched between two layers of cationic surfactants.
the CdS/CdCl2 nanocomposites exhibit semiconducting behaviour, which is similar to bulk CdS, but with a smaller band gap, and a higher photocatalytic activity.
the CdSv X x(OH)y(C n TA)z nanocomposites show a better photocatalytic activity than the bulk CdS, and the best activity is obtained for CdS0.2Cl1.8(OH)2(C12TA)2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electronic properties of the nanocomposite can be tuned in a wide range of values by varying the surfactant length and the sulphide content in the inorganic sheets, and the photocatalytic activity is enhanced by the presence of the surfactants, which act as electron donors.
the nanocomposite CdSv X x(OH)y(C nTA) z, with 2.5 ≤ n ≤ 16 and 0.5 ≤ y ≤ 1.5, can be considered as a model for the study of semiconductor nanocomposites.
the electronic properties of the semiconductor are affected both by the confinement and the interaction with the organic matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to prepare nanocomposite materials in which the inorganic sheets are sandwiched by two self-assembled organic layers, which can be tailored to exhibit semiconducting properties.
, by means of the solid phase/gas exchange reaction, it is possible to obtain hybrid nanocomposites in which the inorganic component has a well-defined stoichiometry.
the photocatalytic activity of the hybrid CdS nanocomposite depends on the concentration of the semiconductor in the inorganic layer.
